answer.label: Written by
answer.sourceLine: This exact line is spoken by Jane in Chapter 34 of Charlotte Brontë’s novel Jane Eyre (1847), as Jane runs after St. John Rivers to mend their quarrel — confirmed word-for-word in the original text.

source.heading: The source
source.excerpt: I have not much pride under such circumstances: I would always rather be happy than dignified; and I ran after him—he stood at the foot of the stairs.
trail: First published 16 October 1847 by Smith, Elder & Co., as Chapter XXXIV of Jane Eyre, under Brontë’s pseudonym Currer Bell.
The line is widely and consistently cited to this chapter across literary-quotation sources, including Goodreads’ quote database ↗.
The full public-domain text is also available via Project Gutenberg ↗.
source.excerptNote: Spoken by Jane in her own first-person narration, describing her decision to chase after St. John Rivers and reconcile.
source.rightsNote: Jane Eyre was first published in 1847, well over a century ago, and its text has long since entered the public domain in the United States.

author.heading: About Charlotte Brontë
author.bio: Charlotte Brontë published Jane Eyre in 1847 under the pseudonym “Currer Bell,” and it became an immediate sensation for its frank first-person voice and its heroine’s insistence on emotional honesty over social convention. She was the eldest of the three Brontë sisters to survive into adulthood as published novelists, alongside Emily and Anne.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The line appears near the end of Jane Eyre, after Jane has refused St. John Rivers’s proposal of a loveless missionary marriage. The two argue and coldly part; Jane’s sister-figure Diana urges her to go make peace with him.

Jane’s narration reads: “I have not much pride under such circumstances: I would always rather be happy than dignified; and I ran after him—he stood at the foot of the stairs.” It is a small, human aside — Jane choosing warmth and reconciliation over wounded pride — that has outlived its plot context to become one of the novel’s most quoted lines.
